targets.authors: Wakslak, C. J., Trope, Y., Liberman, N., & Alony, R.
targets.title: Seeing the forest when entry is unlikely: Probability and the mental representation of events.
targets.evidence_quote: C. J. Wakslak, Y. Trope, N. Liberman, and R. Alony (2006), Seeing the forest when entry is unlikely: Probability and the mental representation of events, Journal of experimental psychology: General, examined the effect of manipulating the likelihood of future events on level of construal (i.e., mental abstraction). Contrary to the original empirical findings, we present two close replication attempts (N = 115 and N = 120; the original studies had N = 20 and N = 34) which failed to find the effect of likelihood on construal level.
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to the original empirical findings, we present two close replication attempts (N = 115 and N = 120; the original studies had N = 20 and N = 34) which failed to find the effect of likelihood on construal level.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors give an overall failure verdict for both attempts.

reasoning: Two new samples re-test Experiments 4 and 5 from one paper. Meta-analysis adds no replication targets. Quotes normalize PDF line breaks.
